title: readOnlyDirs are not deterministically read-only at the cortex layer
finding: readOnlyDirs are appended to --add-dir (which grants access) while write-prevention is delivered only by the preamble - unless Write/Edit are denied via tool policy for that session. So a read-only directory is not deterministically write-protected at the cortex layer. Recommendation: fold into the F1 deterministic path-guard: enforce read-only as a code check on Write/Edit/Bash-write targets, not prose.

OS/arch/kernel/bun-version/cortex-commit were never recorded at capture time and are not reconstructable — do not infer them from the machine running this backfill, or from the cortex commit named in this case's `fix` field (that documents the FIX, not the verification environment). `substrate` (coding harness) is also left `null`: this case was in fact authored during a Claude Code session — commit 2173581 carries a `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5` trailer, and the later environment-attestation commit 94e6598 carries a `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_...` trailer, both consistent with Claude Code — but neither is a captured substrate stamp, so this is recollection backed by circumstantial commit evidence, not a record. Left `null` rather than asserted `claude-code`, per this corpus's own no-guessing rule. environment_digest and environment_provider_digest are `null` for a reason that postdates this case entirely: the field was added when the infrastructure factory's environment contract landed (environments/README.md), and no factory-built machine existed when this case was captured. There is nothing recorded and nothing reconstructable — a digest cannot be inferred after the fact from a machine that was never fingerprinted, which is the whole point of it being a digest. This case stays on the unpinned-baseline count until it is re-established on a factory VM.

expected: A path inside a configured readOnlyDirs entry must deny Write/Edit/NotebookEdit (and Bash write-shaped commands) as a code-level check, while still permitting reads of the same path — read-only must mean read-only, deterministically, not as an instruction the model is asked to obey.

fix.summary: EBH-1b: wired readOnlyDirs distinctly through the dispatch seam (config -> dispatch envelope -> listener -> cc-session) so decidePath's write-deny branch actually receives a non-empty readOnlyDirs set instead of it being flattened into allowedDirs before reaching the hook. F6 'goes live' on this PR per the hardening ledger; the write-deny mechanism itself (decidePath in path-guard.hook.ts) landed with EBH-1 (PR #2355).

verification.note: Spawns path-guard.hook.ts with a readOnlyDirs-scoped fixture directory and asserts: a Write into that directory is denied, while a Read of the same path is allowed.
